dct_description_sm: Yukon Government's (YG) climate change adaptation efforts began formally in 2009 with the inception of the Yukon Government Climate Change Action Plan and a clear articulation of adaptation as a key government priority. With the addition of Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC), Northern Strategy Trust Fund, and other partnerships, YG was able to mobilize key adaptation projects across the territory. The overall intent was that effective climate change adaptation projects become mainstream activity for YG departments and the communities they affect thereby offering effective climate change adaptation approaches to all Yukoners. The Yukon Government chose several of Yukons best proposals for adaptation projects and put them forth when applying for AANDC funding. This particular project addressed the fact that in Yukon scientific research is often undertaken, however much of the knowledge gained through that research is not easily shared with the general public. Within the Whitehorse community, and in various other Yukon communities there is growing anxiety around the impacts of climate change and the realization that although they can choose more environmentally friendly practices, there will still be impacts and they will need to adapt. This project aimed to communicate information pertaining to climate change adaptation to Yukon residents.
